gal-local-situation: The Weil group is GlobalTheory.WeilDeligne.Weil h = weilSub A (normV w), a subgroup of Gal(Omega/E) cut out inside the decomposition group of A by the condition ActsAs (sigma(z)^(q^b) = z^(q^a) modulo the maximal ideal of A); deg is a - b. It is the local Weil group realized inside the global Galois group, not an abstract local Weil group. The wild inertia group P_A is not a separate declaration: it appears as the explicit valuation condition inside UpperTheory.GalS.TmW and UpperTheory.GalStar.Sqf, and as Formalism.MainNotions.BlochKatoReduction.IsWild inside IsTameWD.
gal-local-artin: GlobalTheory.LocLanglands.IsLocalArtin, fields surj, cont, ord_eq, factor, glob. The normalization ord(a(sigma)) = -deg(sigma) sends geometric Frobenius elements to uniformizers. Condition (4) quantifies over every art satisfying IsGlobalArtin.
gal-local-artin-unique: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.artEx proves ArtEx, the existence and uniqueness of a local Artin map, from GlobalTheory.localArtinExists_holds and global Artin reciprocity (uniqueness uses injectivity of the global Artin map on local ideles). This is local class field theory in the normalization of Definition gal-local-artin; it is the same as the published statement.
gal-weil-deligne: WDRep h V requires every rho(sigma) to be semisimple, so these are Frobenius-semisimple Weil-Deligne representations; WD h is the quotient of Sigma n, WDRep h (Fin n -> C) by isomorphism. Sp(l) is WDRep.sp with eigenvalues spEig and N = shiftEnd. Tensor products use N (x) 1 + 1 (x) N and duals -N^dual (WDRep.tensor, WDRep.dual). det x(sigma) is (eig x sigma).prod.
gal-wd-classes: Monodromy-free is WD.mono0; irreducible is IsIrrWD (the Weil group representation rho is irreducible); tame is IsTameWD (rho trivial on IsWild elements) or, equivalently by semisimplicity, UpperTheory.GalS.TmW (characteristic polynomial (X-1)^n on wild inertia), which is the form used in the Galois statements; abelian is UpperTheory.GalStar.Tor, stated through LocalGlobalAboveLAlt.Triv (characteristic polynomial (X-1)^n on commutators). The equivalence with 'direct sum of characters' is a consequence of semisimplicity noted in the text and is not a separate declaration. Multiplicity-free tame part is UpperTheory.GalStar.Sqf.
gal-wd-galois: GlobalTheory.WeilDeligne.wdOf chooses a class x with IsWDOf iota r x if one exists, and is the trivial representation (WDRep.diag of 1) otherwise; IsWDOf.unique shows the class is unique. IsWDOf asks for a continuous surjective t : I_A -> Z_l (IsTameChar), a nilpotent N with r = exp(t N) on an open subgroup of inertia (IsMonodromy), a degree-one phi, and a Frobenius semisimplification (IsFrobSS) of g |-> r(g) exp(-t(inePart g) N). The existence of these data for continuous r (Grothendieck's monodromy theorem) is cited in the text; the statements of this chapter use wdOf as defined, default value included.
gal-p-adic-hodge: The l-adic Hodge theory is stated relative to axiomatized period-ring packages: P : LocPrime l (rings B and B_dR with Galois actions, Frobenius, filtrations and period data for every finite extension of Q_l), AI : LocAinf l P (an embedding of A_inf), a witness of Nonempty (LocTied l P AI) (isomorphisms of these rings with the source's constructions Per.Bcris l and Per.BdR l, compatible with all the structure), and a bridge Bw : LocBridge identifying D_A with the Galois group of a finite extension K_w of Q_l with E dense in it (so bridges exist only at places over l). IsCrysAt, IsdRAt, IsPstAt and IsJumpsAt (multiplicities of the jumps of the filtration at an embedding of K_w induced by tau) are defined relative to these data, and every statement of this chapter quantifies over all packages and bridges. GlobalTheory.Pst.wdAt is the Weil-Deligne representation attached by wdPst to D_pst when IsPstAt holds and the trivial representation otherwise. The text describes these as Fontaine's notions; the agreement of every normalization (for instance the sign convention of Hodge-Tate weights, here jumps of the filtration) with Fontaine's has not been checked beyond reading the definitions.
gal-irreducible-classes: IrrGL k = Sigma n, IrrCl (GL (Fin n) k), which includes degree 0. Supercuspidal is IrrGL.IsCusp (degree > 0 and IsCuspidal). HasSupport is the Bernstein-Zelevinsky support (IsCuspSupport). IsL m pi says that pi is the cosocle (IsCosocle: the unique irreducible quotient) of a product of the representations IsLSeg attached to the segments of m in an order IsOrderedForm. That every element of IrrGL is a Langlands quotient is UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.Pr.exh, used in the proofs of Theorem gal-llc-exists and Proposition gal-llc-unique. Depth zero is DZ, nonzero K_1-fixed vectors with K_1 = SplitWeil.KOne.
gal-good: GoodCusp y : y.1 = 1, or (there is a continuous Q_g -> E_w) and y = y0.tw chi with y0 having nonzero KOne-fixed vectors. Good x : some supercuspidal support of x consists of GoodCusp elements. At a place where E_w is not isomorphic to any Q_g (ramified over Q, or of residue degree > 1), the only good supercuspidals are characters. The plan's paraphrase 'depth-zero supercuspidals over Q_g' omits the twists by arbitrary smooth characters, which are included.
gal-green-datum: A Green datum is the list of hypotheses of UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.TypeLaw (packaged elsewhere as the structure UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.Ext). TypeLaw takes t in the inertia group of E' (Ine (F := E') A) and expresses the residue of a'(t) as red x for x in O_E' with |a'(t) - x| < 1; the text uses the residue map directly and the equality of the two inertia groups, which the source uses in UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.typeIff (DzType.ine_lift). 'Attached' is UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.Names together with IsCusp of the character; 'contains' is GlobalTheory.SerSys.TameGen.Inflates.
gal-llc-laws: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.LawsT a ha rc, fields dim, one, langlands, cusp, nu, absCentral, twist, central, dual, inj, depth, type, in that order as (1)-(12); IsRecT h rc says LawsT holds for some local Artin map. Compared with the published-style characterization GlobalTheory.LocLanglands.Laws (Definition gal-llc-characterization): there is no bijectivity, no condition on epsilon-factors of pairs and no L-factors; cusp is one direction only; twist, central and dual are required only for good representations; inj only when the second argument is good; depth only one direction and only for good representations; and det, prod, supp, sph and sat are absent. absCentral is weaker than central. The type law is not in the published list. The names IsRecT and RecTExists, and the field name localLanglandsExists of UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.OpenLiteratureStatements, suggest the local Langlands correspondence; what is required is this list.
gal-llc-exists: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.recTExists proves RecTExists with no hypotheses; the proof in Section section-gal-local-construction follows it: artEx for the local Artin map, cuspEx for a map r with the laws on supercuspidals (the structure UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.CuspT), GlobalTheory.LocLanglands.exists_isLExt (with Pr.exh and Pr.multi) for the Langlands extension, and extDim, extTw, extDual, extInj, extDepth for the laws; law (12) is obtained through UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.typeIff from the type field of CuspT, using DiscreteGroups.sglob.DzLc.isCuspidal_of_inflates. It is Alpoge's construction, not a published theorem: it is related to the local Langlands correspondence of Harris-Taylor and Henniart only on good representations, and there only conditionally (Remark gal-llc-scope). On supercuspidals that are not good the value is the placeholder (J n).lpTw (e x) of Lemma gal-placeholder and Lemma gal-exponent, which depends only on the degree and on the absolute value of the central character: the map is not injective there and not compatible with twists or contragredients there. OpenLiteratureStatements has a field named localLanglandsExists of type RecTExists, filled by this theorem in UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter_of_row. The published-form statements GlobalTheory.Published.LocalLanglandsExists and GlobalTheory.Published.LocalLanglandsGL appear in the source only as hypotheses; we found no proof of either. Role changed from standard to new.
gal-depth-zero-parameter: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.parUniq proves ParUniq; Par a y V is the list irr, dim, tame, central, type (TypeAt, equivalent to the type law at y by typeIff). Part (1) follows UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.tameUniq: step (a) is pair_of_gen, with t_0 a tame generator (GlobalTheory.MemTame.exists_tameGenAt), phi = (frob h)^(-1) of degree -1, the relation from Tame.conj_eq_pow and the generation statement mem_of_tame_generator_frobenius; step (b) is PositivityTheory.Rg.DzCount.st1a (ExactPer q n z); step (c) is eigenvalue_iff, which the Lean applies to the eigenvalue z^(g^(n-i)) of M' rather than to z; step (d) is st1b, with basis_side for the bases (G^j v); and step (e) is the second half of pair_of_gen, with irreducible_monodromy_zero. For (2) it uses typeEx (a depth-zero supercuspidal contains a cuspidal type), orbit_of_sums (the comparison of eigenvalue sums), nameLaws (Green's theorem in the form of Theorem lit-green-cuspidal) and detByType (two irreducible representations containing cuspidal types with the same character and having the same central character are isomorphic). These representation-theoretic facts are proved in the source; the text cites them to Carayol. Green data exist by UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.extEx and the residue map is surjective by resEx.
gal-llc-unique: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.recTUnique proves RecTUnique with no hypotheses. The proof follows the source: uniqueness of the local Artin map (artEx), par_of_laws and parUniq for twists of depth-zero supercuspidals, the laws twist and one, and Pr.exh with goodSeg for the reduction to the supercuspidal support. This is the precise sense in which the laws determine a correspondence: on good representations only.
gal-llc-characterization: GlobalTheory.LocLanglands.Laws a ha eps rc together with IsDeligneEps eps (this pair is IsRec h rc). The epsilon condition HasPairEps is stated for a supercuspidal pi of GL_{m+1} and any tau of GL_m, with Whittaker functionals and invariant integrals on GL_m, at the centre and without L-factors (which are trivial for such pairs). Item (8) combines the fields sph and sat; the exponent -d(sigma) is that of WDRep.diag applied to the inverses of the Satake parameters. This is the source's rendering of the published characterization of Harris-Taylor and Henniart; we have not checked every normalization (Whittaker conventions, the sign in the functional equation, Satake normalization) against the published one.
gal-llc-of-rec: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.isRecT_of_isRec has the hypothesis hD : GlobalTheory.Published.DepthZeroTypeInertia, which is the statement (T) of the text, and concludes IsRec h rc -> IsRecT h rc via lawsT_of_laws. DepthZeroTypeInertia is a definition that appears in the source only as a hypothesis (for instance as the field depthZeroTypeInertia of several literature bundles, and through GlobalTheory.Mem.LiteralAutomorphy.LitN in UpperTheory.V.Z.Desc.P.toTL); we found no proof of it. GlobalTheory.Published.LocalLanglandsGL is likewise never proved. The proposition is therefore conditional twice over: it assumes (T), and it concerns maps with the published characterization, whose existence is not proved. The plan's paraphrase 'every map satisfying the laws agrees on good representations with the local Langlands correspondence' combines this conditional statement with Proposition gal-llc-unique, of which only the latter is unconditional. Its plan role is changed from standard to new: there is no published source for the laws, and the proof is a comparison of the two lists.
gal-llc-scope: This remark has no Lean counterpart. It records the logical relation between the unconditional statements (Theorem gal-llc-exists, Proposition gal-llc-unique) and the conditional one (Proposition gal-llc-of-rec).
gal-polarized: GlobalTheory.CuspRep.CuspSub is a nonzero irreducible submodule of smooth cusp forms on GL_a(E)\GL_a(A_E) stable under Op E a (the finite adelic group, the unitary group at infinity and the Lie algebra); E is assumed totally complex. CG.infChar chooses the multiset m with HasInfChar (eigenvalues of the operators cap tau u) when one exists and is replicate a 0 otherwise. IsRegAlg is unfolded by CG.isRegAlg_iff. PolarizedPair is the sign condition chi.locInf v (-1) = (-1)^a and DualIsConjBy pi (compNorm chi) = Paired (pi.twist (chi o N)^{-1}) pi conjOp. This agrees with the definition of a polarized pair in Barnet-Lamb, Gee, Geraghty and Taylor as far as we have checked.
gal-compatible: UpperTheory.GalStar.AwayB x y, fields dim, tor, tame0, with IsQpBig w n: there is a continuous Q_g -> E_w with n = 1 or 16 n^2 < g. This is the only form of local-global compatibility asserted in this chapter: clause (2) is full compatibility but only for abelian monodromy-free y, and clause (3) compares only the monodromy and the characteristic polynomials of inertia elements. The source also has the version UpperTheory.GalStar.Away without the bound on g (IsQp only), which is what the source proves (see Theorem gal-galois-representations-any-rc).
gal-attached: UpperTheory.GalStar.PropsB Rc pi iota r wt HT, fields cont, ss, away (AwayB with wdOf), weights, weights_conj, above (UpperTheory.GalStar.AboveB with fields crys and nice, nice using wdAt). The above-l clauses quantify over all period-ring packages and bridges (Definition gal-p-adic-hodge). Compared with the published-form structure GlobalTheory.GalOfCusp.IsGalRepOf, PropsB omits the field pol (r^c isomorphic to r^vee times cyc^{1-a} times the l-adic character of chi), omits the field pure (purity: the Weil-Deligne representation twisted by wt/2 is tempered at every place prime to l), replaces away (IsWDOf iota r (rc ...) for every rc with IsRec, that is full local-global compatibility at every place prime to l) by AwayB, and replaces IsAttachedAbove by AboveB.
gal-galois-representations: UpperTheory.GalStar.Row0b Rc. The main proof uses it with Rc = IsRecT, under the names UpperTheory.One.M.Row and UpperTheory.Gal.Int.recT; Chapters tate-shafarevich and assembly take it as a hypothesis (UpperTheory.One.vwin_of_row, UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter_of_row).
gal-galois-representations-any-rc: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisLocalGlobalStrong_recParameter : Row0b recT, with recT = IsRecT. It is weaker than Barnet-Lamb, Gee, Geraghty and Taylor, Theorem 2.1.1 (which rests on Shin, Chenevier-Harris and Caraiani): there is no polarization of r and no purity; away from l, local-global compatibility holds only in the two cases of Definition gal-compatible, and above l the theorem gives crystallinity with Hodge-Tate weights at places where pi is spherical and potential semistability with compatibility only in the same two cases. 'Strong' in the name refers to the form Row0b and not to full local-global compatibility. The source proves the slightly stronger Row0 recT (UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisLocalGlobal_of_geometry_lift applied to geoOne_holds and UpperTheory.TP.K.tLiftK), in which the tame clause needs only E_w isomorphic to Q_g, with no bound g > 16a^2; Row0b is derived from it by Row0.row0b. Use: UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter applies everyCharacter_of_row to this theorem, which puts it in both fields caraianiLocalGlobalDual and galoisRepOfPolarizedPairLit of UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.OpenLiteratureStatements (both of type UpperTheory.One.M.Row = Row0b IsRecT) and passes it to UpperTheory.One.vwin_of_row. The published-form statements GlobalTheory.Published.CaraianiLocalGlobalDual (for conjugate self-dual cohomological pi: IsWDOf for every rc with IsRec at every place prime to l, and potential semistability with wdAt equal to rc(pi_w) at every place over l) and GlobalTheory.Published.GaloisRepOfPolarizedPair (IsGalRepOf, with polarization and purity) are definitions that appear in the source only as hypotheses; we found no proof of either. So the field names caraianiLocalGlobalDual and galoisRepOfPolarizedPairLit claim more than the statement that fills them. Role changed from standard to new: it is Alpoge's theorem, built in Sections section-gal-seed-construction and section-gal-construction, whose proof follows galoisLocalGlobal_of_geometry_lift. Construction (coreAll_of and rest in IntegralStructures/Development.lean): seeds from the etale cohomology of PEL unitary Shimura varieties (Theorem gal-seed-representations; GlobalTheory.UPel.HT.Datum is a PEL datum of unitary type, and Hodge-Tate weights come from a holomorphic Lefschetz formula and Kodaira-Spencer, KSAll); interpolation in congruence families with pseudo-characters in the manner of Chenevier-Harris (UpperTheory.Gal.Lim.limFinOdd_of, through GlobalTheory.T.isPseudoCharacter_of_approximatedByTraces); theta lifts to definite unitary groups of large rank (Theorem gal-theta-lift-large-rank); descent of conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations of GL_a to definite unitary groups (UpperTheory.Gal.Desc.descOffT, by a trace formula argument); cyclic base change (Theorem gal-cyclic-base-change, as UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Inp.ac); gluing of representations defined over infinitely many CM extensions (UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Core.PatchOne, GlobalTheory.SatSysPatch.patch); and local-global compatibility from spherical places and an Iwahori-level argument (galoisCompat_unlinkedSupport_of_spherical, localGlobalCompatAtIwahoriFixed_of_unlinked). In the text-based closure of this declaration (about 157,000 declarations) no name refers to Igusa varieties or to Taylor-Wiles patching: the names containing 'patch' are the gluing step above or unrelated lemmas, and those containing 'kottwitz' belong to a fixed-point count used for the holomorphic Lefschetz formula.
gal-galois-scope: The translation of the hypotheses uses only the laws dim, one, langlands and cusp of LawsT and the fact that Sp(l) has nonzero monodromy for l >= 2 (WD.not_mono0_lpSp). The remark is a consequence of the definitions and has no separate Lean statement.
gal-cyclic-base-change: GlobalTheory.Published.ArthurClozelStrongTC, proved by UpperTheory.Gal.AbelianGaloisNormality.strongTC_holds (used as UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Inp.ac). The hypothesis is: for every eta with IsNormChar M eta (eta != 1, eta^p = 1, and eta(varpi_v)^f = 1 at almost all places u of M with residue degree f over v), SelfTw fails (the Satake parameters of pi are not stable under multiplication by eta(varpi_v) at almost all v). The conclusion GlobalTheory.GalCut.IsLift has the fields sat, inf, loc of the text. Compared with Arthur and Clozel: the Lean states the lift at unramified places through Satake parameters, at infinity through infinitesimal characters, and at places of local degree one through an isomorphism of local components; it says nothing about the local base change at places of local degree p. By strong multiplicity one, the hypothesis is equivalent to pi not being isomorphic to its twist by a nontrivial character of K^x/N(M^x), so the statement is a consequence of their theorem (existence and cuspidality of the base change, with its local properties at unramified places, at infinity and at places of local degree one).
gal-definite-unitary: GlobalTheory.UnitaryBC.UA E n = UJ (conjAd E) 1, the unitary group of the identity form inside GL_n(A_E). Automorphic forms are IsAutFormU (continuous, left invariant under ratU, open level in finU, finite under infU), representations IsAutRepU. Local components are IsCompAlong U (locU n w) (cLoc w); Satake parameters GlobalTheory.CongL.SatU with GlobalTheory.LFun.HasSatGL (Hecke eigenvalues satEig = q^{j(n-j)/2} e_j(B)); unramified is IsUnramU; weights are HasWeightAt U tau lam, with GlobalTheory.Branching.sqRep lam (the module nablaSq) restricted along cEmb tau. The text calls this nabla(lambda) and does not fix its highest-weight convention.
gal-base-change-definite: UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.baseChangeN proves PositivityTheory.Rg.BcN.BaseChangeIsobaricN (also named GlobalTheory.Published.BaseChangeIsobaricTransfer). The conclusion is IsBaseChangeN with fields pos, discrete (IsDiscrete: square-integrable modulo splitCentre), csd (CsdAsc: P unitary, IsNormalised, IsCsd, and AscEmb V P d, an embedding into indForms, the forms induced without the modulus character from P twisted by |.|^{(a-1)s_j}; as we read indForms, this is normalized induction from P|det|^{-s_j}, so V is a Speh representation embedded in the induced representation with increasing exponents), loc, inf, sub, unram, inert (through HasSatAt and bcParam), split, weight. This matches the form of Labesse's theorem (with the hypothesis that E/F is unramified at all finite places), as the mapping notes record for BaseChangeDefiniteUnitary; we have not compared every normalization. This theorem is used on the branch of Chapter tate-shafarevich (UpperTheory.One.vwin_of_row); the Galois branch uses a related descent (UpperTheory.Gal.Desc.descOffT).
gal-good-base: UpperTheory.TP.W.GoodK (cm, galois = HasK, unram, std = IsStd, inert, psiP) on a Base (psi, emb, m_alpha, m_beta, P, tau, v1, tau1). The fields m_alpha, m_beta, v1, tau1 of Base are not constrained by GoodK and do not enter Theorem gal-theta-lift-large-rank; the text keeps them in (1) and says so. (2) is WeilTensorModels.IsCartan (theta^2 = 1, theta^T M conj(theta) = M, Re((theta x) . M conj(x)) > 0 for x != 0) and GlobalTheory.AdelicU.IsSplitBasis (u in O_v^n iff beta u lies in splitLat t L, the image of latLoc L v under splitProj t, which is the O_v-span of the vectors (t(x_i))_i for x in L). (3) and (4) are Spc (J, L, theta, bas) with J = 1 and IsHerm (cj E) B n 0, resp. J = delta * 1 and IsSkew (cj E) B d 0: herm/skew, sig (signature (n, 0) of J, resp. of i J, at every infinite place, automatic for J = 1 and equivalent to i tau_v(delta) > 0 for J = delta * 1), lat, dual, cartan (IsCartan (J.map (emb w)) (theta w), resp. IsCartan (I * J.map (emb w)) (theta w)) and bas (IsSplitBasis (B.tau v) L (bas v) for v in P). Spc.bas has a matrix at every finite place; only those at P are constrained.
gal-theta-lift-large-rank: UpperTheory.TP.tLift_holds_k proves TLift_k (verbatim the same statement as UpperTheory.TP.TLiftK, which UpperTheory.TP.K.tLiftK proves from it). The conclusion IsLift asserts that U' is automorphic, has the weights of IsLiftWt, and is related to U by the local theta correspondence (LocPair, with the Weil representation GlobalTheory.SplitFlip.omA) at every place of F split in E. It does not assert that U' is the global theta lift of U, and it says nothing at places of F that are not split in E. Relation to the literature: weaker than what the global theta correspondence in the stable range gives. By Li, the theta lift of U to the unitary group of W is nonzero for d large, and the lift then has the properties listed; the theorem here asserts only the existence of some U' with these properties. It is proved in the source from a collection of theta-kernel statements (UpperTheory.TP.Tools_k), not by citing Li or Harris-Kudla-Sweet.
gal-seed: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Div.VBase iota d U rho: Continuous, IsSSRep, ESAt at all but finitely many places w with UsPl d w and l not in w for every B with SatU U w B (with algSat a q_w B = q_w^{(a-1)/2} B), and HTRichEx rho a. ESAt asks rho trivial on inertia and rho(sigma^{-1}) annihilated by prod (X - iota^{-1}(q^{(a-1)/2} b)) for every arithmetic Frobenius sigma. Lacunary is GlobalTheory.RoadWGeo.Lacunary. The dimension of rho is not tied to a.
gal-seed-representations: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.geoOne_holds proves GeoOne, through geometric_realization_of_weight_one = geoOne_of_parts steps_holds (kodaira_spencer_of_weight_one weight_one_geometric_realization) Pl.planEx_holds. The hypotheses are FieldOK E l d, x^2 = -d, NonSplitSet T, Apart v' w0, OneK x w0 v', AutOffT T U, GlobalTheory.CongW.TyEll E l a w0 U, SphOffU w0 S U, SatU U v' B for some B, and LacWtAt iota v' U; the three conclusions are (a), (b), (c) of the text, with JumpsOcc and PhiKilled (whose eigenvalue condition is stated through GlobalTheory.RoadU.satWD). This is Alpoge's statement, not a published theorem. The proof in Section section-gal-seed-construction follows geoOne_of and packEx_of; the geometric ingredients (Steps, KSAll, PlanEx) are summarized there with OPEN items. Role changed from standard to new.
gal-depth-zero-facts: The seven items are UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.typeEx (1), DiscreteGroups.sglob.DzLc.isCuspidal_of_inflates with DiscreteGroups.sglob.DzType.lDepth (2), detByType (3), nameCentral (4), twTame (5), UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.Pr.dzs (6) and tameArt (7). All are proved in the archive, not assumed; the text cites them as standard. typeEx is stated for a representation sigma of GL_n(E_w) composed with GL_n(i), i: Q_g -> E_w continuous, and Inflates means a nonzero GL_n(Z_g)-equivariant map from the inflation of tau. We have not compared the Lean proofs with Moy-Prasad or Bushnell-Kutzko; the statements are the standard facts in the form used.
gal-tame-inertia-character: Items (1)-(4) are UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.extEx, resEx (whose second half is the structure TameSys: pos, normV_eq, rank, surj, isOpen, wild, frob), resBase and, for (4), tameRecAll together with resIndep. In the Lean the map t -> \bar a'(t) is any homomorphism R with Ext.Res R (R t is the residue of an x in O_{E'} with |a'(t) - x| < 1); resEx shows one exists. The number field of (1) comes from GlobalTheory.T.exists_unramified_totallyComplex_ext_with_unity_roots, which also makes E' totally complex. The proofs of resEx and resBase were read at the level of their main steps, which the text summarizes as local class field theory.
gal-induced-parameter: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.indEx proves IndEx. The proof builds the space per n b of functions f: Z -> C with f(j+n) = b f(j), b = (-1)^(n-1) c, with I_A acting by eta_j and phi^m by shifts (rho0), shows smoothness and semisimplicity (isSmooth_inducedParam, isSemisimple_inducedParam) and transports to C^n. Irreducibility uses that the eta_j for j < n are distinct (single_mem). The monodromy operator is 0.
gal-depth-zero-parameter-exists: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.parEx proves ParEx; the proof follows it: typeEx, extEx, resEx, nameLaws (Green), the characters eta_j = theta^(g^(j mod n)) o R, indEx with c = omega(a(phi)), then the determinant via nameCentral and resBase, and the type condition via isoUniq, resIndep, nameLaws and tameUniq.
gal-parameter-operations: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.parOne, parTw and parDual. parOne also records that chi o a is irreducible of dimension 1 with determinant chi o a, the twist and dual formulas for characters and injectivity of chi -> ofChar chi; parTw needs chi tame (TameChar: trivial on units u with |u - 1| < 1). The type part of parTw uses the twisting lemmas DiscreteGroups.sglob.DzTw (isRegularChar_mul, twFD, char_twFD) for the character theta * (chi_0^{-1} o N).
gal-good-map: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.goodMap proves GoodMap. The relation 'fits' is the private Rel; its uniqueness is rel_unique (cases ofChar_eq_of_tw_eq, twist_eq_of_tw_eq), existence on good supercuspidals is rel_of_good, and r_0 is Classical.epsilon of Rel, so its values off good supercuspidals are arbitrary.
gal-placeholder: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.junkEx, from the private junkData and UpperTheory.tameInertiaCharacter_frobenius_conj_eq_pow. gal-crystalline-test-algebras: A test algebra is CrystallineSemistableComparison.PAlg (a perfect O_C^flat-algebra, pFlat-adically complete, pFlat a nonzerodivisor) with PAlg.IsTest = AIC and VAL; the untilt is PAlg.U = W(A)/(xi) with th, and A_cris(A)/l^nu is PAlg.Acr nu, the quotient by l^nu of Acr0, the W(A)-subalgebra of W(A)[1/l] generated by the xi^k/k!. gal-crystalline-realization: Item (1) is an EtFam e with e.Good, of which the fields red, phi and nat are used here (Good also contains equi, cup, one and c1); its existence is CrystallineSemistableComparison.E.etMap, from Main.etale_comparison_map. gal-realization-edge-map: Item (1) is E.Probe.Pts.et for i = 0, chosen (pick) as the additive map satisfying IsEt: some a with Rep x a and Res.Edge of Pts.glob a. Its existence and uniqueness are EtSpec, proved as etSpec from resGood (exact rows, from kapSpec, kapBij, resZero and resSplit, the last from resLoc, locSplit and lcCover), stEx and edgeUniq (existence and uniqueness for the staircase St), repBasic and resZero. The proof follows the archive's staircase St (Res.St; the book's staircase from w to z): fact (i) is stEx (stEx_of_stCol), fact (ii) is stAdd, fact (iii) is stUniq, and the independence of the representative is edge_unique with edgeUniq_of, through Res.VB; the row exactness used is StCol, from resGood (left exactness of sections, resZero and kapBij, at degree 0, and resSplit above). gal-realization-locally-constant: lambda_A is E.lcA A n, chosen (pick) as the additive map satisfying IsLcA. LcIdem (TiltIdem.lcIdem, through PAlg.IsTest.idem, which uses the integral closedness of A^sharp in A^sharp[1/l] and RL.idem_au) gives the idempotents of (1), and LcSpec (lcSpec_of_lcIdem) the formula of (2) and multiplicativity. Naturality and reduction are LcNat (LcNatProof.lcNat), stated as in the text: B a test algebra, a ring map phi : A -> B with PAlg.PdOk phi (the dpw k of W(phi)(xi) lie in B.Acr0, which gives PdOk.acr on A_cris/l^n) and g : A.Ug -> B.Ug with g(sharp e) = sharp (phi e) on idempotents. The proof follows lcNat: the phi(e_a) are complete orthogonal idempotents (CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.map), hg identifies the primes, and LcSpec with PdOk.acr_toAcr and WittVector.map_teichmuller gives the sum. gal-realization-eta: eta_nu is E.eFam, that is eM: (lcMor ...).pull j composed with (pts H r M (identity) n).et 0 j, for the probe E.probe of the identity functor of El(M.P), whose schemes are Spec A.Ug with A.Ug = A^sharp[1/l], and the points E.geomPt into gb M, the base change of X to PadicAlgCl l (the algebraic closure of Q_l, here bar K). The archive defines it for every intermediate field K of PadicAlgCl l over Q_l, with OK l K the elements of K of norm at most 1, and every Model l K, a scheme with a morphism to Spec O_K; the book defines it in the same generality, as (2)(e) of Lemma gal-realization-period-ingredients needs it. The roots of unity r : Roots l of the probe play no role for i = 0.
gal-realization-duality: CrystallineSemistableComparison.EtSide for G = Model.Sm, with fields cup_ex, fin, dual (Model.Dual d for Model.Conn d: connected generic fibre, smooth of relative dimension d) and comp; proved as UpperTheory.Gal.KunnethLefschetz.Top.etSide_sm_holds (core_holds.etSide_sm). The book cites Poincare duality (SGA 4, Expose XVIII; Milne, Etale Cohomology, Chapter VI) for what the archive proves through its own Kunneth-Lefschetz development.
gal-realization-period-datum: An abstract form of the data used by UpperTheory.Ru.crystallineComparison.injAbs: R = per l K (A = A_cris, B = B_dR, P = B_dR^+, with Per.Facts), a Dat with Laws (here dat Amp, whose A-side M.MA is the limit of the H^j(X^sharp, A_cris/l^n) with cup products, and whose H is M.HA false), an EMap (the limit of the eta_nu, from ePin), a BMap b (beta; b.inj and b.surj give (1), b.cup and b.one the multiplicativity) and a PMap p (kappa; lin, lin' and act give (2), cup gives (3) with the products cupR on D^j = HdR M.q j, and fin the finite dimension). Item (4) combines e.c1, b.c1, first_chern_class_unique and p.c1 (IsU is a unit of B_dR^+), as in IsVal.top and pow_rep. The archive's data have further fields (the filtration fil, the module H' with Frobenius, the charts Ch M given by line data, the morphisms Mo) that the injectivity argument does not use. Its H is a GAlg: modules N j over A_cris, maps act j sigma that are only additive (no action law, no compatibility with products), a cup relation with cup products existing by Laws.cup_ex, and a unit predicate one, with x^d formed by IsPow. The book's H^j with products, a unit and additive maps sigma is this; for the H = Model.HA false of Lemma gal-realization-inputs the cup relation and the unit are those of limAlg, formed level by level.
gal-realization-injectivity: The argument of UpperTheory.Ru.crystallineComparison.inj_conn for a connected model, with the periods of exists_val (IsVal, fields smul and spec) and IsVal.van, IsVal.equi, IsVal.cup and IsVal.top (with pow_rep). The archive's conclusion is sum_k q(f(v_k)) i(c_k) = 0 in B_dR. injAbs reduces a general model to connected ones through EtSide.comp and Laws.refine; the book does this in the proof of Theorem gal-crystalline-realization(2).
gal-realization-descent: UpperTheory.galois_equivariant_tensor_descent_of_prime_power_units, with C = B. The archive turns the hypotheses on c into IsLocalization (powers t) and proves the statement in aux through the coordinates of a basis of FractionRing W tensor L (coords), the bound N = sup a_i and loc_ker, which the text follows.
gal-realization-invariants: UpperTheory.Ru.crystallineComparison.InvC B r for every B in PB l K (B_cris) and residue datum r : Res l K, with r.w : W(k) -> A_cris through r.s : k -> O_C^flat; proved as pbInv (PBI.mainC). The book cites Fontaine's computation of the Galois invariants of B_cris, which the archive proves its own way.
gal-realization-frobenius-datum: Assembled from Pb.Fac r N (alpha, beta, e and the fields lin, fac, gal and galT_tmul; phiT, galbeta and nat are not used), BIn M j (item (1) and the Frobenius and Galois compatibilities of the maps betaM, here b_nu, on H = Pb.HL M j = (M.HA true).N j, the limit of the cohomology of divided power thickenings with Frobenius) and keyStep (item (2)), which the archive proves from Pin F M j and absCl. L is Pb.LW r M j, the limit Wc.HS of the crystalline cohomology of the special fibre over W(k), and A_cris tensor L is Pb.AL. The condition on N is what IsRd N rho needs; the archive obtains it from Pb.Mid.TeichmullerCongruence r N by integersResidue_eq_theta_coeff_pow_of_teichmuller, with g = gRes r.
gal-realization-inputs: Item (1) is the fields equi, cup and one of the EtFam with Good produced by Main.etale_comparison_map (fEqui, fCup, fRoot), passed to the limit in ePin (GlueE.eMap). Item (2) is endEx (endEx_of Pb.pSeam), which gives Amp, Per.Facts, EtSide, (dat Amp).Laws, BMap and PMap, with e.c1 from firstChern_family. Item (3) is pinEx (N with f | N, the Teichmuller congruence, F : Pb.Fac r N and Pin F M j) and bInEx (BIn M j, from B.main and GlueBL.lim_surj and lim_inj), combined with absCl in keyStep. All are assembled in cIn and used in UpperTheory.Ru.crystallineComparison.final. The proof of (1) follows the archive. Equivariance is FEquiProof.equi_at: the key step applies EtNat (Lemma gal-realization-edge-map(2)) to the twist functor tM = elTw sigma (pxTw ...), the maps gM = Spec(twUg sigma A) and galMap sigma, with the hypotheses from TwUg (Lemma gal-realization-twist); lM_pull_twMor, from twAcr_lcA, turns the pullback along gM into galMor sigma, whose pullback is Model.galMH sigma. The archive states equivariance for pullback along galMap sigma = 1 x Spec(sigma), which is the action on etale cohomology used in the book. Multiplicativity is eG_cup: EtCup (Lemma gal-realization-cup-staircase, for twPair q 0 0) followed by lcMor_cup, which is MorCup for the ring maps lcA. The unit is FRootCls.eM_rootSys: w is rootSys, the compatible family of rootClass 0 (zetaX M n), the class represented by resGen 0, which for i = 0 is the constant section 1; EtRoot (etRoot_of_spec) computes its image under the staircase, and MorCup gives lambda_*(1) = 1. FCup and FRoot are proved in the archive for all twists i; the book states i = 0, the case that enters EtFam and its fields equi, cup and one. The proofs of (2) and (3) follow endEx_of and cIn. In (2), the line data are Pb.Amp (tautological line data, Pb.pSeam), the period datum is dat Amp with H = Model.HA false, beta = GlueB'.bmap (f_inj and f_surj give condition (1) with exponent 2N, through GlueBL.lim_inj, lim_surj and GlueBE.exists_eps_period_t_unit), kappa from Pb.pmap, and condition (4) combines e.c1, b.c1 (B.firstChern_compatible_l), Laws.first_chern_class_unique (glueL, from E.Main.firstChern_unique) and the field c1 of Pb.pmap (Pb.kap_pow, Pb.pow_ex), as IsVal.top does in the injectivity argument. In (3), H = Pb.HL M j, b_nu = betaM, condition (1) is bInEx (B.main with GlueBL.lim_surj and lim_inj), the compatibilities with phi and sigma are B.compat, alpha, beta and e come from Pb.Fac, and condition (2) is keyStep (Pin with absCl, Lemma gal-realization-frobenius-fixed). What remains open is in Lemma gal-realization-period-ingredients.
gal-realization-period-prism: CrystallineSemistableComparison.P.prism (Auxfc.prism_main), proved with the prism operator Auxfc.hh and the identities htpy_zero and htpy_succ (m'.pullC - m.pullC = d (hh f) on cocycles of positive degree), which the proof follows. cr_pull_eq is the case of functors into a category of thickenings whose natural maps are ring maps (crHom). This is the classical fact that a natural transformation of functors induces a homotopy between the induced maps of nerves; the archive proves it directly.
gal-realization-period-functors: A point functor over O is B.Fn O: a functor Pt from commutative rings to types with a relation Ov (y lies over f) satisfying ov_map and ov_uniq; a map is B.Fn.Map, a natural transformation u with the field ov. F_X is B.schFn q and h_* is B.schMap u hu. F^sharp is Fn.pt kappa, whose value at A is the set of y in Pt(A.U) with Ov y (A.oC.comp kappa); schFn_pt identifies (F_X)^sharp with PX q kappa by definition, and u : F^sharp -> F'^sharp is Fn.Map.pt (schMap_pt). The twist y^sigma is B.ptTw F kappa sigma hsigma, the image of y under Pt of the inverse of twUEquiv sigma A, with hsigma the condition galOC sigma (kappa x) = kappa x; t_sigma is elTw sigma (ptTw ...), and the map sigma of (4) is the pullback along galMor sigma (ptTw ...), whose maps of coefficients are twAcr. For schemes, schFn_ptTw identifies ptTw with pxTw, the twist of Lemma gal-realization-twist(3). In the archive sigma lies in Gal(PadicAlgCl l/K) for an intermediate field K of PadicAlgCl l over Q_l, with no finiteness condition; every such sigma lies in G_{Q_l}, which is why the book applies Lemma gal-realization-twist with Q_l for K.
gal-realization-period-thickenings: The thickening categories are GlobalTheory.LogCris.Thick for the functors B.Lc F kappa k n = F.cr (bs l k n) (kappa_b), for a point functor F (B.Fn), and F = schFn q for an O-scheme. The base bs l k n is (base l).Acr n = A_cris/l^n with the ideal JJ k (PAlg.Fil n 1 for k = false, PAlg.PFil n = (l) + Fil n 1 for k = true) and divided powers DD k, chosen by RL.pd_ex with the property IsPd stated in the book. Thick also carries log data (charts x, v, s), which are empty for F.cr (index set Empty, s = 1), and the condition that l is nilpotent in B, automatic since l^nu = 0 in A_nu; the book leaves both out. The point is an element of F.ptK kappa_b, a pair of the map A_nu/I -> B/J induced by i (by the field w of Thick) and an element of Pt(B/J) lying over its composite with kappa_b, which the book writes as an element lying over the induced map, and for schemes as an O-morphism for the induced structure. H^j_nu(F) is B.Hc F kappa k n j = CH.H (B.Oc ...) j. The maps of (3) are redHc (for every n <= m), galHc (galMorC, for sigma with galOC sigma (kappa x) = kappa x), phiHc (phiMorC, with phiPt the l-th power map frb of B/J), (cmpMor ...).pull and pullHc, all pullbacks along functors omMor (crMor ...). g_nu and g'_nu are B.gT (jE followed by gE, objects gObj), and beta_nu, beta'_nu are B.β = (βMor ...).pull for k = false and true. H^j_infty and H'^j_infty are the limits of Model.HS k j, with the algebra structure Model.HA k (limAlg); beta and beta' are GlueB'.bβ and bβ', the limits of GlueB'.βS. The reduction of H^j(F^sharp, A_cris/l^nu) is the pullback along CH.Mor.ofNatTrans (redEl ...). The divided power filtration of (6) is B.HcFil F kappa k n r j = (pdS ... r).img j, the image of the cohomology of the subfunctor pdS r (T -> T.pdPow r, the book's J_T^[r]) of the coefficient functor; the archive uses it in BMap.surj and PMap.fil and states its properties in Compat (Lemma gal-realization-period-compatible(3)).
gal-realization-period-compatible: Item (1) is B.CompatH (B.compatH: CrisTransition.redHc_galHc, CrisFrob.red_phi_le, redHc_pullHc, CupTrans.redHc_cup, CrisUnit.redHc_oneH, CrisCmp.main), proved with cr_square (identity maps of thickenings, through cr_pull_eq) and with omMor_cup and omMor_oneH (P.cup_pull). Item (2) is B.Compat (B.compat: BetaRed.beta_red with redNat, BetaGal.β_gal with etaGal and twAcr, CrysPhi.phi_beta with etaPhi, BetaCmp.β_cmp, BetaPull.beta_pull, CupBeta.beta_cup and CrisOne.β_one), and the proof follows these. CompatH states that the reductions preserve cup products and units (cup and one), not that the maps sigma, iota_nu and u^* do, nor that the maps sigma compose to an action of G_K; the book states only what CompatH proves. The archive's period datum does not need more: there H is a GAlg (Model.HA false), whose field act is a family of additive maps with no further law, and Definition gal-realization-period-datum asks for the same. Item (3) is the fields red_fil (CrisFil.red_fil) and smul_fil (BetaFil.smul_fil) of Compat; smul_fil asks that (base l).cris n a lie in JJ k (base l) n, the book's image of a in I_nu or I'_nu. Both structures quantify over every ring O, every point functor F (B.Fn O), maps u : Fn.Map F F', kappa, both ideals (k : Bool), and sigma in Gal(PadicAlgCl l/K) for any intermediate field K with galOC sigma (kappa x) = kappa x, with the action galMor sigma (ptTw ...) on the right; the book states this generality. The reductions are taken for all n <= m in N and the levels include 0, where A_0 = 0 and every group is 0; the book takes n >= 1.
gal-realization-period-limit: P.lim_upTo (UpTo s at each level gives UpTo s^2 for the limit), with the passage to powers of t in GlueBL.lim_inj and lim_surj (t = a u and s = a^N). The proof follows P.lim_upTo. GlueBL.lim_surj_fil, the version with filtrations, is not used in the book.
gal-realization-period-t-mu: GroundTheory.PAdicHodge.ACris.exists_periodT_eq_mu_mul_unit, used through GlueBE.exists_eps_period_t_unit for the system GlueBE.eps (a B.Eps: compatible l-power roots e k of epsilon l, with theta([e 0]) = 1 and theta([e 1]) different from 1, and mu = [e 0] - 1). The archive writes t = mu u with u the l-adic sum of elements U_n with (n+1) U_n = (-1)^n mu^n, using exists_mu_pow_eq_pow_mem (mu^(l-1) = l c with c^l in l A_cris^0), and shows that u is a unit by isUnit_of_sub_one_mem_jacobson_bot. The book gives the result of this computation.
gal-realization-period-de-rham: HdR q j = H (smFun X q) j, the cohomology of GlobalTheory.LogCris.Thick for the base infBase K (R = K, I = 0 with trivial divided powers, p = 0) and the point functor ptFun X q; for p = 0 the admissibility condition of Thick says that J is nilpotent. Cup products and unit are Pb.cupK and Pb.oneK (CH.mulP and CH.oneH of thA), pullbacks are pullR (smMor), and powers are Pb.powK. The archive also defines a Hodge filtration FilR, used in the fields fin, top and fil of PMap, which the book does not need. The name de Rham cohomology is the archive's (HdR); the book uses only the properties stated in Lemma gal-realization-period-ingredients(3).
gal-realization-period-chern: (1) is E.LineData (fields Y, f, sm, surj, u, nat, coc) and E.LineData.pb. (2) is Pb.IsTautologicalLineAt and Pb.IsTautologicalLine, with the transition functions Pb.ratio R N j k = x_k / x_j on the chart where x_j is invertible. (3) and (4) are B.CLift, CLift.r and CLift.coc with B.dlog, in B.IsFirstChernClassOfLineBundle at the base bs l k n with truncation l n (B.IsFirstChernFamily). (5) is E.Lift (units w of A with sharp w = u), Lift.r, E.IsLog, Lift.IsCoc and E.IsFirstChernClassOfLineBundle. (6) is Pb.CLiftK, Pb.plogK and Pb.IsFirstChernDeRham, where InU V T says that the point of T lands in V. The remark in (3) that r(s) - 1 lies in J is proved in the archive with the argument given: CocCls.red_Rf (from red_w, red_um, uq_map and uq_mul) shows that the image of r(s) in (B/J)^x is 1, and CocCls.sub_one_mem turns this into r(s) - 1 in J, for thickenings of Th_nu and Th'_nu; ConeUnit.r_sub_mem (Pb.r_sub_one_mem) does the same for de Rham thickenings. The archive uses it in its proofs about these cochains, for instance that the cochains of (4) are cocycles (CocCls.closed, through dlog_rel); its definitions apply the divided powers to r(s) - 1 without the hypothesis, as the dpow of Mathlib vanishes off J.
gal-realization-frobenius-special-fibre: The residue field, its embedding s into O_C^flat and W(k) -> A_cris are a residue datum CrystallineSemistableComparison.Res (k, rho, s, and r.w), as in Lemma gal-realization-invariants. (1) is the thickening category of Wc.L l (schFn q) rho nu over Wc.bs nu (W_nu = Wc.Wm with the ideal (l) and divided powers Wc.pd, chosen with the property stated), H^j_nu(Y/W) = CH.H (Wc.OM ...) j, and L^j(Y) = Pb.LW r M j, the limit of Wc.HS under Wc.redMor. (2) is a MuMor r M nu (a CH.Mor from Wc.OM to B.Oc ... true nu, semilinear for r.w) satisfying IsMu r M nu N: ring isomorphisms eta equal to the maps tau, DP morphisms carrying J onto J, eta(i w) = i(Pb.Mid.wn w), and the condition on points with the l^N-th power map. The Frobenius of L (Wc.phiS), used in other fields of Pb.Fac, is not needed in the book.
gal-realization-frobenius-fixed: UpperTheory.Ru.crystallineComparison.absCl, which proves AbsCl for every model M, residue datum r, F with IsFr f F and rho with IsRd N rho. X is (gK r M n 0 r.w ...).pull j y, the pullback along gam (objects gObj: A_cris(A)/l^nu with the map iA, the ideal PFil and the point through qq, the book's q_A). Step 1 is gK_succ and gK_iter, Step 2 is absCl_fr (phK, phiA_fix, phK_dp, phK_mk, qq_frob and IsFr), and Step 3 is absCl_rd (IsMu, psi, qq_psi and IsRd), each through cr_pull_eq; the proof follows the archive. The transformations F and rho_N of Definition gal-crystalline-test-algebras(4) satisfy IsFr f and IsRd N.
gal-realization-period-ingredients: Item (1) is B.Main l in the form of Lemma gal-realization-ingredients-bounds: one N for all d and j, every ring O, every point functor with a Zariski atlas (Fn.Atlas d) of dimension d, every kappa, every epsilon, every level and both ideals, with the filtration refinement for I_nu. The main theorem applies it to F_Y through GlueB'.atlas_of (B.P.atlas, Lemma gal-realization-ingredients-atlas-scheme). Item (2): (a) is Pb.isO1_exists, for every ring R and X with IsProjOver (a closed immersion into some projective space over R), and Pb.isTwistingSheaf_pullback, for every ring map R -> R'; (b) is Pb.firstChern_acris_family_exists, for every model (any O_K-scheme) and line datum D with sSup (𝒱D D) = ⊤, the book's condition that Y be the union of the opens over which f has a section; (c) is B.FirstChernCompatible (B.firstChern_compatible_l), for every ring O, O-scheme, kappa, both ideals and families x : ∀ n, Hc ... n 2 that need not be compatible; (d) is E.FirstChernUniqueEtale (E.Main.firstChern_unique, with R.forE for its hypothesis RIn l), for every ring O, O-scheme, kappa and families in the product over nu; (e) is E.FirstChernClassFamily (E.Main.firstChern_family), the field C1 of the family eFam of comparison maps, for every model and line datum. The archive states (b) and (e) for every intermediate field K of PadicAlgCl l over Q_l, with OK l K its elements of norm at most 1, and the book states them so, for a field K' between Q_l and its algebraic closure in C, with eta_nu formed for K' (Definition gal-realization-eta); their proofs do not use that K' is finite. Item (3) is a KapL L with LieComplementChartContDiffAt L from Pb.crystalline_deRham_firstChern_exists (fields lin, lin', act, nat, fil, cup and one; the archive's cupR is cupK by Pb.cupR_eq), with Pb.m_fin for finiteness and Pb.isFirstChernDeRham_exists and Pb.powK_ne_zero for the last sentence. The archive's kappa is one family for all models and tautological line data (KapL Amp, with Amp = Pb.Amp), and so is the book's kappa_{Y,L}; it is 0 on models that are not smooth, where no field asks anything. nat is (d), with (dat Amp).Mo u hu a b = PUnit, so no compatibility of h with the line data; pullH is the limit of pullHc (schMap u hu) and pullR the de Rham pullback along Model.genMap u hu. fil is (e): (dat Amp).fil a j n x says that every component of x lies in HcFil ... false n' n j, FilR M.q j (r + 1) is the set of classes of cocycles with values in pdPow (r + 1), and (per l K).P is B_dR^+ in B_dR, with tB = t. Item (4) is crystallineComparison.pinEx (PinEx, for finite K and every f > 0, the book's f_1): N with f | N and Pb.Mid.TeichmullerCongruence r N (which gives the congruence by integersResidue_eq_theta_coeff_pow_of_teichmuller), F : Pb.Fac r N and Pin F M j; alpha, beta and e are F.α, F.β and F.e M j, (a) is F.lin, F.fac and F.gal with F.galT_tmul (galT agrees with sigma tensor 1 on pure tensors, and both are additive), and (b) is Pin. The proofs of (1) and (2)(a) to (2)(d) follow the archive: (1) is Lemma gal-realization-ingredients-bounds (B.main); (2)(a) is isO1_exists with Lemma gal-realization-ingredients-tautological; (2)(b) is FirstChernClassFactorial.exists_C1H (existsUnique_chern_class_nilpotent_base at each level and chern_class_reduction_compatible; the main theorem supplies the hypothesis by Pb.sSup_𝒱D, Lemma gal-realization-ingredients-tautological(4)); (2)(c) is FirstChernComparison.main, for both values of k, whose steps are lam (the lift Lambda_nu along gG k n G, with hw from u_square and uJ_th), lam_r (r' is the image of [r]), sharp_r (theta([r(s)]) = 1, Step 1), st1 (the hypothesis on x_nu), pull_transport (G^* beta_nu x_nu = G_nu^* x_nu) and isLog_dlog with dd_dxi (Step 3); (2)(d) is EtChern.chern_class_unique_of_lift_and_log, with LineLift.liftEx (sections from RIn.splitU, Lemma gal-crystalline-test-facts(2), and units from RIn.sharp, Lemma gal-realization-ingredients-sharp-units) and isLog_unique, applied to the identity functor (restrict_id_pull). The proof of (2)(e) follows firstChern_family_of_lifts: lineBC is the base change L' (Definition gal-realization-period-chern(1)); LineMap, chern_class_compatible_system and KummerPrimitive.main give the classes x_n with a, h and k (Lemma gal-realization-ingredients-kummer-class); FUntwPf.main puts v_n = x_n cup w_n, with w the family rootSys of FRoot for the twist -1, and uses FCup and CupOne (Step 1); fKum gives the Kummer cocycle (exists_root for the roots omega, hr_eq for r^q, chain_pow and rootPow for z, Step 2), and with r_eq and lcLog its logarithms (Step 3); etale_chern_class_eq_kummer_class identifies its class (Lemma gal-realization-ingredients-kummer-cocycle); fRes, from EtNat, is the restriction along G, and tCo_cls multiplies by t. The archive's roots are the probe roots r.zeta, images of a Roots r whose r.ρ n maps to rootSeq l n, which is the book's zeta_n = theta([epsilon^{1/l^n}]) by EpsRoot. The proof of (3) follows Kap.kap_abs, applied to an approximation system from HT.levSys_ex and a system of truncated periods from Kap.Mo.rhoSys_ex: exists_lim forms the limits through the field cpl of LevSys.Good, ext_P gives their uniqueness, and the fields lin, lin', act, cup, one and c1 come from the fields smul, lin', act, cup, one and c1 of the RhoSys with Lev.Good's iota_lam, toB_K and sigmaB_toB and Per.Facts's sigma_mem; the archive's kappa is 0 on models that are not smooth projective. The proof of (4) follows PinP.pin_fixed: N from PinP.teich_dvd, F from Pb.fac_ex (pin_all for e and alpha, betaP = Fa.beta for beta, lin from Fa.Pin.lin, fac from Fa.Pin.fac with Mid.mu_nu, and gal from Fa.Pin.op with bW_gal and nu_gal, whose argument for equal exponents the book writes out directly), and (b) from PinP.pin_of with PinP.pin_lev. The flatness and completeness of A_cris over W are flatW and adicA. What remains open are the lemmas these proofs rest on. Neither (3) nor (4) is a published theorem, so they are not cited: their statements concern H_infty and H'_infty (cohomology of the categories of thickenings over A_cris/l^nu), HdR (the category of nilpotent divided power thickenings of Y_K) and L^j (the category of all thickenings over W_nu), which the archive does not identify with crystalline or de Rham cohomology. The published comparison theorems related to them: (3) corresponds to the comparison of crystalline cohomology over A_cris with de Rham cohomology over B_dR^+ (Berthelot-Ogus BO83, Faltings Fal89), and (4) to the Frobenius isogeny of crystalline cohomology of the special fibre (BO83); the archive proves each in its own form, which is the form stated here.
gal-realization-kappa-approximations: Part (1) is Pb.Kap.Lev (per l K) (m) with Lev.Good and Lev.CrisOK, for the period ring per l K (A = A_cris, B = B_dR, P = B_dR^+ as the range of BdRp, o the inclusion of K, sigma the Galois action); toB, IB, gammaB, A, I, gamma, iota, lam, sigmaA and sigmaB are tau, J, delta, A, I, gamma, iota, lambda and the sigma_A and sigma_B. Condition (a) is toB_surj, toB_ker, toB_K and pdP_B; (b) is iota_inj, iota_dp, iota_I, IB_eq, iota_O and iota_lam; (c) is sigmaB_toB, sigma_iota, sigma_lam, sigma_O, sigmaB_K, sigma_dp and sigmaB_dp; (d) is lat, LatBase gamma l s for all s at least m (fields tf = TFBase, fg, prime, val, dv, cpl and closed), whose only dependence on s is pdP gamma s = 0, so it is stated for s = m; (e) is Lev.CrisOK, which the archive states separately and proves for every member of the system (HT.levSys_ex). The field pos (1 at most m) holds since the heights are m + 1. pdP gamma r is the ideal I^[r]. Part (2) is Pb.Kap.LevSys with LevSys.Good: L m has index m + 1, and the fields dB_toB, diota, dlam, dO, dK, ddp, ddpB, dsigma, dsigmaB and cpl are the conditions listed.
gal-realization-kappa-approximation-syst: HT.levSys_ex, restated as Pb.levSys_ex': there is S : LevSys (per l K) with S.Good and (S.L m).CrisOK for every m, for K finite over Q_l. Neither the construction nor its statement is a published result. The proof follows levSys_ex: levHyp_ex gives M with LevHyp l K M (fields ok from exists_lattice_bound_integers, cris from acris_mem_lattice_sub, hc from fontaine_lattice_dpow_closed, galT and gal from galois_preserves_t_power_span and galois_preserves_lattice_sub, dIn from lattice_sub_reduction_mem; Lemma gal-realization-kappa-truncations); the system is Lat.levSys h, with L m = Lat.lev h (m + 1) on Bk l (m + 1) = BdRp / t^(m + 1) and A = Lat.A (fk l (m + 1)) (xi0 l) l M, the book's Q_(m+1) and Lambda_(m+1)(M); lev_good and levSys_good verify the fields in the order of the proof, with level_toB_eq_zero_iff_t_pow_dvd, level_filtration_span_t_pow, level_ideal_eq_map, level_galois_isDPMorphism, level_lattice_base (Lemma gal-realization-kappa-lattice-ring), level_system_transition_isDPMorphism and existsUnique_period_of_compatible, and level_xi_mem_ideal_and_theta_compat gives CrisOK. The archive's toB is pk composed with pInv, the inverse of the identification of BdRp with its image P in B_dR. sigmaB_dp and ddpB are HT.dp_of_char, the argument given for sigma_B. The archive's xi0 is [l^flat] - l, the negative of the book's xi; it generates the same ideals and the same lattice rings, since its e_i are (-1)^i times the book's.
gal-realization-kappa-lattice: Lat.η, Lat.dpE, Lat.sub (the closure of range f and range dpE), Lat.A, Lat.IB, Lat.γB (the divided powers RatAlgebra.dividedPowers of the Q-algebra B), Lat.I (IB pulled back to A) and Lat.Hyp: the fields one_le and nil are (1) with m at least 1, gr is (2), dom and val are (3), dv, l0 and cpl are (4), and unit is (5). gal-realization-kappa-de-rham: (1) is Pb.k_fin (k_fin_pf), for q proper and smooth, with a further clause that FilR q j (j + 1) is 0; Pb.m_fin applies it to the generic fibre of a smooth projective model. (2) is Pb.isFirstChernDeRham_exists (isFirstChernDeRham_exists_of) and (3) is Pb.powK_ne_zero (powK_ne_zero_main), for SmoothOfRelativeDimension d q, with ConnectedSpace X in (3); powK q c d is the power c^d. They are related to the finiteness of algebraic de Rham cohomology of proper smooth varieties and to the nonvanishing of the top power of the Chern class of an ample line bundle, but they concern the cohomology of the category of nilpotent divided power thickenings, which the archive does not identify with algebraic de Rham cohomology, so they are not cited. The proof of (1) follows KFin.main (the finiteness half of de_rham_finite_and_filtration_bounded), through KIso, GrAff and GrCechFin with the induction on the filtration (dev); it chooses s = max d_α + j + 1 as the Lean does, although any s > max d_α works for the finiteness. The proof of (2) follows isFirstChernDeRham_exists_of (restriction_bijective_above_dimension, clsK, clsK_res and test_factor); the properness of X is isProper_of_isO1, which the book cites from Stacks, Tag 01WC (Lemma 29.44.5). The proof of (3) follows powK_ne_zero_main = powK_ne_zero_of geo_setup resid_alg firstChern_local_exact, with its inputs stated as Lemmas gal-realization-kappa-de-rham-setup, -residue, -local-exact, -cup, -cech, -transfer and -cone-vanishing. An Eps is a compatible system (e_k) of units of O_C^flat with e_{k+1}^l = e_k, theta([e_0]) = 1 and theta([e_1]) ≠ 1, and mu = [e_0] - 1; as O_C^flat is perfect it is determined by epsilon = e_0, which is the book's epsilon. For a smooth, separated and quasi-compact O-scheme, Lemma gal-realization-ingredients-atlas-scheme (B.P.atlas) gives an atlas of schFn q, which is how GlueB'.atlas_of applies it. Alpöge proves it in this form for point functors with a small presentation (B.Local, local_of: a computation with the Rees module of a filtration, using D.out : D.Out l, a statement about elements of A_inf proved as out_of_rin l (R.forD l)), glued over the atlas (global_of with P.glob, exponent (max over d' <= d of N(d', j+1)) (2j+3)) and passed to each level (level_all, through level_zero and level_pos). The proof states the published counterpart with locators checked against arXiv:1602.03148v3 and arXiv:1905.08229v4: BMS18 Definition 9.1 (A Omega = L eta_mu R nu_* A_inf), Theorem 12.1 (the base change of A Omega to A_cris is the crystalline cohomology of the fibre modulo p over A_cris, for every smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_C) and Lemmas 6.9 and 6.10 (for an invertible ideal I and C with H^n(C) I-torsion-free, natural transformations I^m tau^{<=m} -> tau^{<=m} L eta_I and tau^{>=n} L eta_I -> I^n tau^{>=n} whose composites on tau^{[n,m]} are the inclusions I^{m-n} -> O and I^m -> I^n; the book uses n = 0, m = j); BS22 Theorem 1.8(1) with Theorem 5.2 (the crystalline comparison for prismatic cohomology) and Theorem 17.2 (A Omega_R = phi_A^* of the prismatic cohomology of R over A_inf, for a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra R). These concern crystalline, A_inf-, pro-etale and prismatic cohomology of one smooth formal scheme. The archive's statement is about the cohomology of the category of all divided power thickenings and of the category of test algebras, which the published works do not consider, and the archive does not identify these cohomologies with the published ones. The archive's statement is also uniform: N depends only on d and j, for all point functors with a Zariski atlas of dimension d, which need not come from schemes, and for I_nu the preimage lies in Fil^N. Neither the uniformity nor the filtration is in the published statements. The relation is: the same comparison, stated for different cohomology theories, in a uniform form that no published statement covers; the citations give the published counterpart, and the lemma itself is an open step.

The relation is: the same class, in a different cohomology theory.

(1) is UpperTheory.ConvolutionTheory.C.IsSummand (IsSummandOf: a closed, invariant, nonzero and irreducible subspace of cuspidalL2). (2) is Dp.Carries: Cm.carrier pi = formsIn mu V, the elements of centralCuspForms (invariant under centralSection) whose class under clsL lies in V. (3) is SInf: m has n elements and Oinf mu nu (lact (zc tau i) beta) = e_(i+1)(m) Oinf mu nu beta on V for every Haar measure nu on archGroup K n = GL_n(K tensor R), every smooth compactly supported beta and every i; Oinf integrates R through archP, and zc tau i is the image of the Harish-Chandra preimage of esymm (i+1) under the tau-holomorphic embedding IsJ. (5) is At S V Lambda t, and T.AtAE asks it off some finite S. (6) is a PositivityTheory.Rg.Tf.Core.Twist theta with IsGalTwist sigma theta: theta.e is the entrywise action of galAd sigma on normOneGL, and theta.U phi is phi composed with the inverse of theta.e almost everywhere (U_spec).
gal-depth-zero-lift-stable-parabolic: (1) is bcInf and bcSat (resDeg is the inertia degree, the residue degree of w over v). (2) is UpperTheory.ConvolutionTheory.Datum (r at least 2, positive d i with sum n, Haar measures mu i and IsSummand (mu i) (V i)) with Datum.Pt S Lambda t: there are lam, m and B with At (mu i) S (V i) (m i) (B i), Lambda tau the sum of the m i tau shifted by lam i, and t w the sum of the B i w multiplied by absNorm w to the power -lam i for w not in S. (3) is T.OffAll K n Lambda t, that is OffFam K n SE S Lambda t for every finite S with SE the places of M over S; its two clauses are (i) and (ii). (4) is T.LiftPlus for one pi: WeakBC pi.HasSat (R.sumSat Q) for a nonempty finite family Q i in CG M (m i) with every m i at least 1.
gal-depth-zero-lift-stable-carried: (1) is Dp.exCusp (ExCusp, existence and uniqueness), (2) is Dp.exSummand (ExSummand: Carries pi V if and only if the carrier of pi lies in centralCuspForms and V is the closure of its image under clsL), (3) is Dp.exTwist (ExTwist, with an IsPow character absC E z; the Lie element oneL acts on pi by the scalar of letter_centralExponent), (4) is Dp.sInfIff and Dp.sSatIff, (5) is the first two components of T.carryLift (its private atEx, from exCusp, sInfEx and the existence of Satake parameters at almost all places), and (6) is Dp.isoEq, from UpperTheory.V.Af.cuspMultOneGL. The Lean proves (1), (2) and (6) its own way; the text cites the decomposition of the cuspidal spectrum (Gelfand, Graev and Piatetski-Shapiro, with Harish-Chandra for the passage to cusp forms) and Shalika's multiplicity one theorem. The published results are that the cuspidal part of L^2 decomposes discretely, with finite multiplicities, into irreducible representations whose smooth vectors are cusp forms, and that each irreducible representation occurs in it at most once. The Lean's (1) and (2) are the special case for GL_n over a totally complex field, phrased as a bijection between cuspidal summands of L^2_n(K) and cuspidal automorphic representations invariant under the positive real scalars; its (6), that isomorphic cuspidal automorphic representations are equal as spaces of functions, is a reformulation of multiplicity one.
gal-depth-zero-lift-stable-twist: (1) is Dp.conjIff (ConjIff), stated for a twist theta whose map theta.e is the entrywise action of an adelic ring automorphism s with IsGalAd sigma s; P o sigma isomorphic to P is Cusp.ConjIso P sigma, which quantifies over such s (unique by Dp.galCentral and K.adUnique). The proof follows conjIff: UpperTheory.CBC.SConjSpaceC_holds for the cuspidal representation P o sigma, Dp.conjCarries (V' carries P o sigma if and only if theta V' carries P), Dp.isoEq, Dp.exSummand and the uniqueness in Dp.exCusp. (2) is the last component of T.carryLift, which takes theta from K.galTwistEx and passes from sigma to its powers by induction (conj_iff, pull_trans), as in the text.
gal-depth-zero-lift-stable-summand: (1) is T.LiftAll, proved by Sph.liftAll = T.liftAll (T.liftStep (T.coreLift ci Sph.gm)), by strong induction on n. (2) is T.CoreLift, proved by T.coreLift ci Sph.gm, for every twist theta with IsGalTwist sigma theta. Both are Alpöge's own and are the core of UpperTheory.ConvolutionTheory.cbcc, by which the Lean proves Theorem gal-depth-zero-lift-base-change. The text cites the cyclic base change of Arthur and Clozel (Chapter 3), proved by comparing the full trace formulas: (1) is their existence of the base change of a cuspidal representation, an isobaric sum of cuspidal ones, and (2) follows from it with strong multiplicity one and multiplicity one as the statement says, using only clause (i) of the hypothesis. The Lean's comparison also needs clause (ii), to remove the noncuspidal spectrum over K, so the statement keeps it. The Lean's forms are weaker than the published ones: (1) asks only for a family of cuspidal representations over M whose Satake parameters add up to those of the base change at almost all places, without local base change at the other places, and (2) asks only for a theta_sigma-stable cuspidal summand with the base-changed parameters off a finite set. Remark gal-depth-zero-lift-stable-summand-comparison describes the Lean's proof.

The deduction of (1) is T.liftStep and T.liftAll.

Item (5): shLift s f, defined with a chosen gamma such that incl gamma is conjugate to nrm s delta (IsNorm); for class functions the value does not depend on the choice. gal-support-shintani: KillsOn (fun _ => True), proved by killsTrue from KillsOn (fun a => a.D = []) (killsNil, from KillsAll = GlobalTheory.T.shintani_lift_kills_product_of_cusp_forms, proved by GlobalTheory.Shin.DescentAll.kills_liftAll), LiftHc (GlobalTheory.Shin.shLift_hc_eq_hcTw), KillsHc (GlobalTheory.Shin.HcIso.kills_hcTw), NormEx (GlobalTheory.T.every_element_is_norm), LiftOk, JDEq, JDChar and LiftDet. The Lean uses theta on AlgebraicClosure k' and pullTheta iota theta on AlgebraicClosure k; the text uses one Theta. The induction on D follows killsTrue. For D empty the proof follows GlobalTheory.Shin.DescentAll.kills_liftAll: an induction on L whose step rewrites J (p :: L) by J_cons, applies LiftHc, splits liftAll (p :: L) into the lifted pairs of p followed by liftAll L (with J of an append given by harishChandraProductCuspidalGL_list_properties), and concludes by twistedHarishChandra_isotypic_part (KillsHc) from the single-cuspidal lemmas of Lemma gal-shintani-cuspidal and the induction hypothesis; the base case L = [] is GL_0, with isInCharacterIsotypicPart_self. KillsAll is stated for any nontrivial s in Gal(k'/k) with [k':k] prime; KillsOn takes s to be z -> z^q. Items (a), (b), (c) and (d) of the proof are LiftHc (Lemma gal-shintani-hc), LiftDet with NormEx, KillsHc, and kills_self. Remark gal-shintani-remark keeps the derivation of the case D empty from Shintani's theorem, which the Lean does not use. Items (1) to (3) of Lemma gal-depth-zero-lift-support use only the case D empty.
gal-shintani-situation: The data of the Lean's Shintani lemmas: fields F, F' with Algebra F F' and Finite F', an automorphism s : F' =_F F' such that every automorphism lies in zpowers s, galAct (the entrywise action of Gal(F'/F) on GL_n(F')), incl : GL_n(F) -> GL_n(F'), nrm s delta = nrmG (galAct) s (finrank F F') delta, IsNorm s delta gamma = IsConj (incl gamma) (nrm s delta), and InPar a x for the block upper triangular condition. KillsOn takes s to be z -> z^q, which satisfies the hypothesis.
gal-shintani-twisted: (1) is GlobalTheory.Shin.hcTw t a b alpha beta n, defined for any ring endomorphism t of a field F and any a, b and n, with the normalizing factor the inverse of the number of InPar a elements of GL_n(F); hc is hcTw (RingHom.id). The text defines it for a finite field, as Lemma gal-shintani-parabolic(2) assumes, and for a + b = n: for n different from a + b the Lean's blocks tlG and brG are the junk values of toG (1 when the block is not invertible), and the book never uses that case. (2) is GHat F F' n, the semidirect product of GL_n(F') by F' =_F F' acting through galAct. (3) is GlobalTheory.CuspGL.psi S V g, defined by invariantSubspaceMobiusInverseRec, with psiG S n on matrices and chG S n x = S (charpoly x); psi of rootSum theta c is the function psi_c of Definition gal-support-level-zero(3).
gal-shintani-norm: (1) is galoisTwistedNormGL_basic_properties (GlobalTheory.Shin.NrmBasic.main): the fixed points of galAct s are the image of incl, incl is injective, the twisted conjugation formula (nrmG_twConj), delta s(N delta) = N(delta) delta (mul_map_nrmG), and multiplicativity under commuting conjugates (nrmG_mul). (2) is exists_coboundary_of_norm_one_in_subalgebra (GlobalTheory.HilbertNinety.hilbert90_matrix_subalgebra_norm_one), proved as in the text with galoisDescent_sum_basis_smul_ker_bijective for Galois descent and nonempty_linearEquiv_of_pi_fin_pow_finite (if M^l and N^l are isomorphic finite modules, so are M and N) for the cancellation; the text cites Serre and the Krull-Schmidt theorem for these. Serre's Proposition 3 [Ser79, Chapter X, Section 1] is H^1(Gal(K/k), GL_n(K)) = 1 for a finite Galois extension of fields, which is Galois descent for K-vector spaces with a semilinear Galois action. The Lean's galoisDescent_sum_basis_smul_ker_bijective (Shin.galoisDescent_semilinear_bijective) is the corresponding descent for a finite field extension k'/k whose Galois group is generated by s, an s-semilinear map T on a k'-vector space with T^[k':k] = 1, and a basis of k' over k, which the Lean proves itself. The cancellation of l-th powers of finite modules over any ring (PowCancel.cancel_pow) is a consequence of the Krull-Schmidt theorem for modules of finite length [Lam01], also proved in the Lean. The count in (2) is card_twistedNorm_one_mul_card_fixed_units (GlobalTheory.Shin.card_nrm_one_mul_card_fixed). (3) is norm_map_surjective_finite_field (GlobalTheory.Shin.NormSurj.nrm_surj_adjoin). (4) is conjugate_into_adjoined_algebra (GlobalTheory.Shin.isNorm_exists_twistedConj_adjoin). gal-patch-index-two: GlobalTheory.IndexTwoPatch.main, stated as in the Lean: Gamma a topological group, k an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 that is a topological ring, eta : I -> Hom(Gamma, Z^x) injective with open kernels, each r i continuous and semisimple on ker(eta i), hypotheses (1) and (2) on traces, and the conclusion on traces for cofinitely many j. Related to, but not a special case of, Sorensen, Galois representations attached to Hilbert-Siegel modular forms, Doc. Math. 15 (2010), Section 4.3, Lemma 1. Sorensen takes Gamma = Gal(Fbar/F) for a number field F, cyclic extensions of prime degree and l-adic coefficients, assumes the family S-general, and concludes that rho restricted to Gamma_E is isomorphic to rho_E for every E. His hypotheses (a) Galois invariance and (b) compatibility are equivalent to (1) and (2) here by Brauer-Nesbitt and Clifford's theorem, and for semisimple representations equality of traces is isomorphism. Steps 1 to 6 of his proof use only that the family is infinite (S-generality enters in Step 7) and give the isomorphism for every E linearly disjoint from M E_1, which for quadratic extensions excludes finitely many E; the steps are group-theoretic (Zariski closure of the image, Clifford theory for a cyclic quotient). That is the statement here for Galois groups, which is the case the book uses (Lemma gal-patch-quadratic). The Lean proves the abstract statement its own way: it extends each r i to rho i on Gamma (GlobalTheory.T.exists_extension_rep_index_two_of_trace_invariant, from (1)), fixes i0 with eta i0 nontrivial and the finite set B of quadratic characters chi with a nonzero matrix X such that rho_i0(g) X = chi(g) X rho_i0(g) for all g (finite_quadratic_characters_in_adjoint'), and for every j such that eta j, eta j eta i0 are outside B and eta j is neither 1 nor eta i0 builds rho'_j agreeing with rho_i0 on ker(eta i0) and with the trace of r j on ker(eta j) (conj_on_inter_quadraticKernels_of_trace_eq, intertwiner_zero_of_character_twist, exists_rep_agreeing_on_kernels, from (2)). For one such j1, rho = rho'_j1; for every j for which also eta j1 eta j and eta j1 eta j eta i0 are outside B, which is all but finitely many, rho and rho'_j have the same trace on Gamma (intertwiner_zero_of_quadratic_twists, using the six characters eta j1, eta j, eta j1 eta j and their products with eta i0). The proof follows LateralTheory.DivDb.plus_of (DivPlus.lean), which proves the variant DivPlus whose last conclusion is a family of intertwiners T_j, T'_j with sum T'_j T_j = 1; goal_of turns these into Covers. gal-congruences-eigen: GlobalTheory.T.eigenvector_small_sub_finite_eigen_approx_inequality, proved by GlobalTheory.Cong.eigen_small_sub_finite_approx by induction on the integer polynomial P, as in the text; the approximating set is the image of the eigenvalue families of the v_i.
gal-congruences-forms: Algebraic forms are GlobalTheory.DefU.algForms W, linear maps from W.Sp to the automorphic forms autU, equivariant for infU; the weight W is Wt.ofFam lam, which uses lam at the embedding chosen for each infinite place. Fixed by C is UpperTheory.Gal.Gen.fixedBy, A_lambda(C,P) is part W C P (a supremum of finPart meet fixedBy over the AutSub with property P), a level is IsLevel, a level away from w0 is GlobalTheory.Cong.IsLevelAway, K[J] is lev K w0 J, type (lambda,K) is OfType and the action of a family of Hecke operators is ActsBy, with opOf (RU E a).
gal-congruences-dense: Density is UpperTheory.Gal.Gen.Dense, l-integrality is Loc.IntL (the bound uses the weight sizes wtSizeOver over the places u over l with cLoc u g different from 1, and lying over is GlobalTheory.CongW.OverPair), a gauge is FramedX, and Phi-generic is GenAt. The Lean also uses the global condition IntW, with the whole weight size in the exponent; it implies IntL, and Loc.frame accepts either.
gal-congruences-gauge: UpperTheory.Gal.Gen.Loc.frame, from DenomBdd, RhoBound, LatFacts and LevelEx, with kappa from Loc.kappa; frameW_pf is the version for IntW. The gauge is b g x = rhoK W (M g) x with M g = (cAll g)^-1 kappa g and x ranging over the vectors with coefficients of norm at most 1.
gal-congruences-density: UpperTheory.Gal.Gen.ToPolyX, proved by toPolyX_pf from PartFacts (the decomposition of part W K P into finPart components) and the eigenvector lemma; the existence of the form f is GlobalTheory.T.exists_algebraicForm_weight_level_smooth_at_place. gal-congruences-weight-family: The combination of FamEx (famEx_of, from NeatLev, EllC, Twist, TwistBd, Kap0, Pieces, DeltaNear and FamOf), FamProj (famProj_of, from SumRep) and FamWt (famWt_of, from FamOff and FamSum). The Lean states FamEx for a family B with Fam tau W K nu d B, the structure listing automorphy, K-invariance, the equivariance at infinity, the highest weight rule and the exponent bounds, and splits B with FamProj; the text states the combined result that top_of uses, with F_V' the functions Ft V of top_of. The properties of famOf are the self-contained computation FamOf.
gal-congruences-weights: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Cong.WtLacEx = WtTo GapWt, proved by UpperTheory.Gal.Wt.top_of from FamEx, FamProj and FamWt. GapWt a mu says that the multiset (a-1)/2 minus the infinitesimal character of mu, which is {k - mu_k}, is lacunary (GapJ). The weight nu is N times mu0 with mu0 k = -(a+1)^k and N = (a+1)(4d+a)+1, and lacunarity is gapJ_of_near. The Lean's conclusion has mu equal to lambda at every tau that is not OverPair for v'; CongUW4 keeps only the weaker SameWtOff, which excludes the embeddings over w0 as well.
gal-congruences-section: UpperTheory.Gal.Gen.Ell, proved by ell_pf from the group-theoretic EllGrp (ellGrp_pf, the choice of representatives of double cosets); the finiteness of the stabilizers uses GlobalTheory.T.isOfFinOrder_of_compact_conj_mem_unitaryRationalPoints.
gal-congruences-type-character: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Cong.EllSt, proved by exists_ellType: for a at least 2 by GlobalTheory.CongW.TypeExists.exists_type_surj, with J the kernel of reduction modulo l^m and the character through the trace against a lift of a matrix with no invariant subspace over the residue field; for a = 1 by exists_congruence_surj. Supercuspidal is GlobalTheory.SmGL.IsCuspidal, the vanishing of the Jacquet modules of all proper parabolic subgroups, proved through jacquetModuleCoinvariants_subsingleton_of_char_conj.

Alg is alg_pf from HB (ultrametric duality on a finite product, hB_pf) and GroupDet (groupDet_pf, from TriMat, the unitriangular form of the regular representation of an l-group modulo l, and DetLow, the bound for det(A + cB) by the rank of A).
gal-congruences-negligible: UpperTheory.Gal.Gen.NeglAt with Negl, proved by neglAt_pf from GlobOp and Small (small_pf, from SymEx, StarEx, NullZero and DensCont). GlobOp is globOp_pf from LocOp, which the Lean proves (locOp_pf, planch_pf) from Macdonald's formula for the zonal spherical functions (RFormula) and the orthogonality of the resulting functions against the Plancherel density (RInt, GammaInt). Count is count_pf from CountCore (countCore_pf: the Hilbert-Schmidt bound HS with WBound), Cover (class number finiteness and coset representatives), Sep (sep_pf, from RatFin) and PartFacts.
